deep.reconstruction:
The page is a handwritten sheet bound into a printed elementary algebra text (the printed left margin is §§54–60 on roots and imaginaries). It has three independent pieces.

(1) Partial ODE integrated in x only. For d²z/dx² = φ(x,y) = P(x,y), integrate twice in x with y as a parameter. Each integration constant becomes an arbitrary function of y:
z = ∫dx ∫P dx + x·f(y) + F(y).

(2) Linear second-order equation in x, again with y as a parameter: z_xx = P·z_x + Q, where 'ubi P et Q sunt functiones ipsorum x, y'. The steps (made explicit by me) are:
- Put w = z_x. Then w' = P·w + Q is first-order linear.
- So w = e^{∫P dx} [ ∫ e^{-∫P dx} Q dx + f(y) ].
- Integrating once more gives Gauss's result:
z = ∫ e^{∫P dx} ( ∫ e^{-∫P dx} Q dx ) dx + f(y) ∫ e^{∫P dx} dx + F(y).
His 'I:' abbreviates Integrale. The nested Euler-style notation ∫e^{∫Pdx}dx∫e^{-∫Pdx}Qdx means the outer integral of e^{∫P} times the inner integral.

(3) Riccati equation, written a·dy/dx² = yy + x^n. The following lines show the intended equation is a·dy/dx = y² + x^n.
- Substitution: y = -a·t'/t. Then a·y' = -a²t''/t + a²t'²/t², while y² = a²t'²/t².
- The t'² terms cancel, leaving the linear equation a²t'' + x^n t = 0.
- Power-series ansatz: t = A + B x^{n+2} + C x^{2n+4} + …
- Comparing coefficients gives a²B(n+2)(n+1) + A = 0 and a²C(2n+4)(2n+3) + B = 0, etc.

Gauss then writes two fundamental solutions:
- t = 𝔄[1 - aa x^{n+2}/((n+1)(n+2)) + a⁴ x^{2n+4}/((n+1)(n+2)(2n+3)(2n+4)) - …]
- + B[x - aa x^{n+3}/((n+2)(n+3)) - a⁴ x^{2n+5}/((n+2)(n+3)(2n+4)(2n+5)) …]

Finally y = -a t'/t, with 𝔄 now denoting the ratio of the constants:
y = [a³x^{n+1}/(n+1) - a⁵x^{2n+3}/((n+1)(n+2)(2n+3)) … + 𝔄(a - a³x^{n+2}/(n+2) …)] / [(1 - aa x^{n+2}/((n+1)(n+2)) …) + 𝔄(x - aa x^{n+3}/((n+2)(n+3)) …)].
This is the general solution of the Riccati equation as a quotient of two power series with one arbitrary constant.

Correct version (mine), with the coefficients that actually follow from a²t'' + x^n t = 0:
- t₁ = 1 - x^{n+2}/(a²(n+1)(n+2)) + x^{2n+4}/(a⁴(n+1)(n+2)(2n+3)(2n+4)) - …
- t₂ = x - x^{n+3}/(a²(n+2)(n+3)) + x^{2n+5}/(a⁴(n+2)(n+3)(2n+4)(2n+5)) - …
- y = -a(t₁' + 𝔄 t₂')/(t₁ + 𝔄 t₂).

Next page (66) continues with series reversion into continued fractions, so this is a working sheet on series and integration methods.
errors: The Riccati equation is written a·dy/dx² = yy + x^n, but the substitution line computes a·dy/dx; the dx² is a slip (or an ambiguous notation) for dx.

The powers of a in the series are inverted. From a²t'' + x^n t = 0 one gets B = -A/(a²(n+1)(n+2)), C = A/(a⁴(n+1)(n+2)(2n+3)(2n+4)). Gauss writes aa and a⁴ in the numerators, which corresponds to t'' + a²x^n t = 0 (i.e. a replaced by 1/a). The coefficient recursion he writes down, aaB(n+2)(n+1) + A = 0, itself gives the 1/a² form.
In the second (odd) series the third term should have sign + (+x^{2n+5}/(a⁴(n+2)(n+3)(2n+4)(2n+5))). Gauss writes '-'. The x^{2n+5} factor is also omitted.
In the numerator of y the third term lacks its power x^{2n+3}.

Sign slip in the numerator: since y = -a t'/t and the denominator contains +𝔄·t₂, the numerator should contain -𝔄·a·t₂' = -𝔄(a - a³x^{n+2}/(n+2)) in Gauss's convention. He writes +𝔄(a - …). This is not absorbable, since the same 𝔄 appears in the denominator with a + sign.
Minor: the lowercase 'p' in z_xx = p z_x + Q is the P of the formula; the series are truncated ('&c.') without a general term.

results.what: Double integration of z_xx = φ(x,y) with arbitrary functions f(y), F(y) as integration 'constants'
results.modern_name: Integration of a PDE reducible to an ODE in one variable (arbitrary functions as constants)

results.what: General solution of z_xx = P z_x + Q via reduction to a first-order linear equation and integrating factor e^{-∫P dx}
results.modern_name: Integrating factor / variation of constants for first-order linear ODE, applied to w = z_x

results.what: Linearization of the Riccati equation a y' = y² + x^n by y = -a t'/t to a² t'' + x^n t = 0
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (1760s), d'Alembert; special Riccati equation studied by Riccati and Daniel Bernoulli (1720s)

results.what: Two power-series fundamental solutions of t'' + c x^n t = 0 in powers of x^{n+2}, and the Riccati solution as a ratio of series with one arbitrary constant
results.modern_name: Frobenius-type series solution; equivalent to Bessel functions t = √x·Z_{1/(n+2)}(2x^{(n+2)/2}/(a(n+2)))
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (series solutions of the Riccati equation, Inst. calc. int. II, 1769)

deep.surprise_reason: All three items are textbook 18th-century material (Euler's Institutiones calculi integralis): integrating factors, the Riccati linearization, and series solutions. This looks like an early study or working sheet. The slips (inverted powers of a, sign errors) suggest quick exercise work rather than original research. Nothing goes beyond Euler.

checkable.asserts: Substitution y=-a t'/t turns a y' - y² - x^n into -(a² t'' + x^n t)/t; result should be 0.
Corrected even series solves a²t''+x^n t=0 up to O(x^{3n+4}); the only remaining term is x^{3n+4}/(a⁴…), here x**10.
Gauss's coefficient aa (instead of 1/aa) does NOT cancel the x^n term unless a=1, exhibiting the slip.
Corrected odd series (with + on the third term) solves a²t''+x^n t=0 up to x^{3n+5}.
Bessel-function closed form of the linearized equation (numerically ≈0).
w=z_x = e^{∫P}(∫e^{-∫P}Q dx + f) solves w'=Pw+Q, so z=∫w dx+F gives Gauss's formula for z_xx = P z_x + Q.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'Von (ddz/dx²) = φ(x,y) ist das Integral'. There is a struck/overwritten letter before φ; the integral line reads z = ∫dx∫Pdx + x f:y + F:y (P standing for φ).
'p ∂z/∂x' should read 'P ∂z/∂x' (same P as in the solution formula).
'I:' is an abbreviation of 'Integrale' (or 'Int.'), not a separate symbol.
'ubi P et Q s. fctnes ipsorum x, y' = 'ubi P et Q sunt functiones ipsorum x, y'.
The leading coefficient of the first series is the Fraktur constant 𝔄, not lowercase 'a': t = 𝔄(1 - aa x^{n+2}/(n+1.n+2) + …).
Second series third term: the manuscript shows '- a⁴/(n+2.n+3.2n+4.2n+5)' without the power x^{2n+5}; it begins with a struck character before n+2.
